subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership be accepted as a first-class authorization boundary for triggering OpenClaw agents and tools?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but the requested behavior changes who can invoke agent/tool workflows from Slack and the issue itself identifies Slack Connect/private shared-channel caveats.

options.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
options.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned normal routing, slash/action authorization, security audit docs, Slack Connect caveats, and tests while keeping existing defaults unchanged unless separately approved.

options.title: Reject private-channel trust
options.body: Keep explicit Slack channel IDs as the only non-open group authorization path and document private/shared channels as insufficient for trust by themselves.

options.title: Defer to broader identity work
options.body: Let the broader conversation-audience work decide personal/team/shared semantics before adding a Slack-specific policy value.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
recommendation.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned normal routing, slash/action authorization, security audit docs, Slack Connect caveats, and tests while keeping existing defaults unchanged unless separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and is the strongest available security/product routing candidate in the related Slack authorization history.
